notToBeConfusedWith.name: White rum
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Rum is usually distilled from molasses; rhum agricole is distilled from fresh-pressed sugarcane juice under Martinique's AOC rules and is bottled higher-proof and more vegetal than most white rum.

generalSubstitutes.note: Molasses-based and usually lower-proof, so the drink loses the grassy, vegetal note agricole is chosen for and comes in noticeably weaker.

forms.label: Blanc
forms.sourceNote: FoodData Central carries no rhum agricole record. Rhum agricole blanc is typically bottled between 50% and 55% ABV under Martinique's AOC rules; 50% is taken as the representative bottling. Energy is scaled from Alcoholic beverage, distilled, rum, 80 proof (public domain, 231 kcal/100 g at 40% ABV) in proportion to alcohol content, since an unsweetened spirit's energy is a function of its ethanol alone. Density is density-classes.json's spirit-high class (0.93 g/ml), the one for overproof spirits at 50% and above, rather than the 40%-ABV rum record's own.
